title: Normalization of the global boundary of the pro-etale support triangle
statement:
Fix a finite commutative ring $A$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with exact $i_*$ and $i^*,j^*$ as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Put $i^!_0M=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ [def-pur-flasque-support], and write $S=Ri^!_0$ on $D^+$, with its support counit $\epsilon:i_*SK\to K$ as in [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle]. Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, represented by a bounded-below complex of injective module sheaves $I$. Let $\beta:Rj_*j^*K\to(i_*SK)[1]$ be the third arrow of the support triangle constructed from this injective resolution with the cone convention [def-pur-support-triangle, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived global sections identify that entire triangle with
$$R\Gamma_Z(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(U,j^*K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_Z(X,K)[1],$$
where the first term is identified by the sectionwise support kernel and the third by the direct-image/sections comparison. More precisely, the sequence of complexes of $A$-modules
$$0\to\Gamma_Z(X,I)\to I(X)\to(j^*I)(U)\to0$$
is degreewise short exact, $j^*I$ computes $j^*K$, and its usual cochain connecting homomorphism equals $H^q(R\Gamma(X,\beta))$ under these identifications. For every $q\in\mathbf Z$, a cocycle $c\in(j^*I)^q(U)$ and a lift $b\in I^q(X)$, that homomorphism sends $[c]$ to $[db]\in H^{q+1}(\Gamma_Z(X,I))$. Thus it is precisely the supported-cohomology boundary $\partial$ of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], with no extra sign. These identifications and the boundary are natural in $K$.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal E=i_*i^!_0I$, $\mathcal B=I$, and $\mathcal C=j_*j^*I$. The supported-kernel comparison identifies $\mathcal E$ with $\ker(\mathcal B\to\mathcal C)$, and the injective support exactness lemma gives $0\to\mathcal E\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{v}\mathcal C\to0$ degreewise. The first map is the kernel inclusion under this comparison, not an arbitrarily scaled map. The support localization theorem identifies its associated cone triangle with the triangle of the statement, with first arrow the support counit and second arrow the open unit.

proof.text: The injective-support global model provides the support adjunction and preservation of injectives by the closed supported right adjoint. Direct images preserve injectives because their inverse images preserve finite limits. For the open inverse image, the published weakly-etale inverse-image injectivity theorem applies to the open immersion. All three additive functors preserve a common lower bound. Apply the bounded-below injective K-injectivity lemma to the three resulting complexes; their right-derived units therefore compute their derived sections.

proof.text: Restriction of an injective module sheaf along the site monomorphism U -> X is surjective: the associated map between free module presheaves on representables is monic, sheafification is exact, and injectivity extends the section morphism across that monomorphism. Evaluate the extension at the identity generator. The supported-sections functor is literally the kernel of this restriction, so the row is termwise short exact. The actual open-section comparison uses the open-restriction comparison and the canonical isomorphism X times_X U = U; the adjunction-unit comparison identifies the evaluated sheaf unit with the specified restriction arrow.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support, injective restriction sequence and first distinguished triangle; pro-etale module specialization using cited ringed-site results

proof.text: The sheaf short exact sequence splits in every degree because its first term is injective. Map these splittings by evaluation at X; the mapped sequence remains short exact. The degreewise-split boundary theorem identifies each cone-to-quotient boundary with localization of the split connecting chain map. Additivity maps that connecting chain map, including its shift comparison, to the connecting chain map of the evaluated splittings. The unit of the unbounded right derived functor commutes with shifts: restrict it to K-injectives, express it through the K-injective equivalence and its unit, and use the equivalence triangle identity; extend along a K-injective resolution. Naturality and shift compatibility of this unit therefore give a triangle isomorphism from derived evaluation of the sheaf triangle to the quotient triangle of the evaluated row, with the three inverse-derived-unit components.

source.place: Tag 014Z, section-canonical-delta-functor, cone-to-quotient construction with third arrow -p composed with inverse(q); definition-cone

proof.text: The actual open-section comparison gives an isomorphism b from the third evaluated sheaf complex to the open section complex, commuting with restriction. The evaluated sheaf row and the sectionwise-kernel row are short exact. Their universal kernels therefore supply a unique first-term isomorphism a commuting with inclusion, with the identity in the middle. The induced morphism of short complexes gives an isomorphism of their canonical quotient triangles. Compose it with the derived-unit triangle isomorphism of step 4. Both cone quotient maps are quasi-isomorphisms by the short exact cone lemma. The cone homology-boundary comparison identifies the homology boundary of the final quotient triangle with the ordinary snake boundary, conjugated by the canonical localization homology comparisons.

source.place: Tag 014Z, section-canonical-delta-functor, cone-to-quotient construction with third arrow -p composed with inverse(q); definition-cone

proof.text: Fix any integer $q$ and a cocycle $c\in G^q$. Step 3 gives a lift $b\in F^q$. Since $v_X(db)=dc=0$, there is a unique $a\in E^{q+1}$ with $u_X(a)=db$. Then $u_X(da)=d^2b=0$ and injectivity of $u_X$ gives $da=0$. In the cone, $d(b,-a)=(db-u_X(a),da)=0$ and $q_X(b,-a)=c$. The third arrow is minus projection, so it sends this cocycle to $a$. Thus the induced boundary sends $[c]$ to $[a]=[db]$ under the kernel identification. Both minus signs are necessary: one in $(b,-a)$ and one in the third arrow.

source.place: Tag 014Z, section-canonical-delta-functor, cone-to-quotient construction with third arrow -p composed with inverse(q); definition-cone

proof.text: The result is independent of choices: another lift $b+u_X(t)$ changes $a$ to $a+dt$, and replacing $c$ by $c+dg$ permits the lift $b+dh$ for any lift $h$ of $g$, leaving $a$ unchanged. Addition and $A$-linearity follow by adding and scaling lifts. This is exactly the usual cochain snake construction for the short exact sequence in step 3. The derived injective boundary normalization identifies that snake boundary with the natural derived supported-cohomology boundary, whose long exact sequence is the one in the support exactness theorem. The kernel functor used there is precisely $\Gamma_Z$, so the map just computed is $\partial$ with no sign change.

proof.text: For a chain map f:I -> J, prove naturality of the first-term identifications by composing with the monic sectionwise kernel inclusion. The normalized inclusion squares and naturality of the sheaf support inclusion identify the two composites. Prove naturality of the third-term identifications by precomposing with the epic evaluated sheaf restriction; the normalized restriction squares and naturality of the sheaf unit identify the two composites. Cancel the monomorphism and epimorphism respectively. The boundary supplied in step 7 is already a natural transformation on the whole derived category, so its naturality is built into the normalized-boundary interface. For exactness at an arbitrary bounded-below derived object, choose an injective representative using the injective homotopy-category equivalence and apply injectiveBoundary_exact.

The triangle comparison fixes every component by the right-derived unit and the sectionwise kernel/restriction squares; its final equality identifies its homology boundary with the usual snake boundary. The boundary theorem uses the existing SupportSequenceBoundary and SupportSequenceExact interfaces for every finite commutative coefficient ring, and quantifies all integer degrees, all injective representatives, all identifications with K, and all cocycle lifts. The real-data open-evaluation and derived-composition isomorphisms identify the third term with RΓ(U,j^*K).
